**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, for a free smooth approximation: a $G$-invariant open subset $U$ of a
finite-dimensional complex $G$-representation on which $G$ acts freely, and
$b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the group is the eventual stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$; existence of the stable value and its independence of the
approximation are supplied by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen free smooth approximation
because the stable Borel value exists and stabilizes by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is consumed exactly through the three cited suppliers, whose
constructions (equivariant descent, injective replacements, Borel stabilization) declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.

actual_current_use_paragraphs:
In branch (CP) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced
modules $J(\nu)$ of
[[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the
normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the
general-field normalization/crystal clauses of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and
[[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]]
(in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by
[[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the
**graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
for $\lambda,\nu\in RP_\alpha$ by
$$[J(\nu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)=[J(\nu):D(\lambda)]_q .$$
Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,\nu})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its
entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy
$a_{\nu,\nu}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd\nu$ (dominance);
equivalently $a_{\lambda,\nu}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in
$(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}(D_\nu)$.

actual_current_use_paragraphs:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In
the point/projective-line geometry with $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_2=\mathbb P^1$,
$d_1=0$, $d_2=1$ and $L_1=k$, $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], let
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let
$\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation
$R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by
$1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then
$\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the
correspondence isomorphism of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has
$[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental
class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the
point corner gives its generator.

**Given:** the Axiom of Choice; the trivial group $G=1$; the base $E=\mathrm{pt}$; the sources
$X_1=\mathrm{pt}$ and $X_2=\mathbb P^1$ with $d_1=0$, $d_2=1$; the proper maps
$f_1:\mathrm{pt}\to\mathrm{pt}$ and $f_2:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$; the objects $L_1=k$ and
$L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$; the unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and the
evaluation $\beta:R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$; and the conventions of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]].

records.prior_actual_use_excerpt: [F3] Assume AC, that $k$ has characteristic zero, and that a product $G$ of complex general linear groups acts algebraically. The same six-operation contract, with the normalized dualizing object satisfying $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$ and $\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$, holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category $D^b_{G,c}$ built from that normalized object, with the same Cartesian pasting and the same properness clause ([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]).
actual_current_use_paragraphs: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be the analytic space of a smooth complex algebraic variety of pure dimension $d$, and let $q:A\to M$, $u:B\to M$ be morphisms of complex algebraic varieties with fiber product $T=A\times_MB$; write $a:T\to A$ and $b:T\to B$ for the projections, so that $qa=ub$ and the square is Cartesian. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor–Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]], [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $\mathrm{ex}:a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of the base-change morphism $u^*q_!\to b_!a^*$ of this square, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel–Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.

The characteristic-zero theorems of this page
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]],
[[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]])
compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis
coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization
[[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]]
reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix
and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally
nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity
adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero
canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number
problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the
boundary recorded in
[[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]]
and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark
records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
